analysis:
Reviewed ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift (head text) and Qwen35TemplateFixesTests.swift (patch, base and head). The error-mapping file already treats .missingUserQuery as a client error: 400 at line 255, .clientError reason at line 63, and .invalidRequest code at line 159. The sanitizedInferenceFailure path (lines 15-34) returns only closed enums, a status code and bounded usage, so no raw error strings reach the wire or logs. This keeps the T-008/TB-002 posture of not leaking engine text. Raw messages are only lowercased and substring-matched in boundedCapacityReason (lines 85-108), never returned. The test file changes are test-only: new tests for Qwen35TemplateFix.validateUserQuery, a pre-render missingUserQuery check via ProviderPromptContractPipeline.tokenize, and a status 400 / invalidRequest / clientError assertion. The existing admission-envelope test now includes a user message so it still passes under the new validation. These changes add no new attack surface and do not touch crypto, attestation, the prefix cache (T-041), keys or authorization.

Limits: the implementation of validateUserQuery and ProviderPromptContractPipeline is not in the supplied units, so its behavior, such as the model-type gating where qwen3_vl_moe and qwen4_exp are not rejected, is only inferred from the tests. The new pre-render 400 for histories without a user query is an availability and validation tightening on consumer-controlled input. It is deterministic and bounded, and does not look like a regression. No findings.
